title: Fourth pillar of Iman – belief in the messengers
intro: “Wa rusulihi” – and I believe in Allah’s messengers.

learn.text: O you who have believed, believe in Allah and His Messenger and the Book that He sent down upon His Messenger and the Scripture which He sent down before.

learn.html: Allah’s messengers are chosen people to whom Allah (SWT) sent His revelation. By Allah’s will they were raised and taught for their mission. Every Muslim must believe in Allah’s messengers.

The first man on Earth, Adam (AS), was also the first messenger: Allah taught Adam, and through him all people, how to live in this world. After Adam, Allah sent messengers from time to time to pass on His revelation. They explained it to people, called them to do good and turned them away from evil.
There were very many messengers – the traditions mention 124,000. Every people had its own messenger. 25 messengers are named in the Qur’an:

items: Adam, Idris, Nuh, Hud, Salih, Ibrahim, Ishaq, Isma‘il, Lut, Ya‘qub, Yusuf, Ayyub, Shu‘ayb,
Musa, Harun, Dhul-Kifl, Dawud, Sulayman, Ilyas, Al-Yasa‘, Yunus, Zakariyya, Yahya, ‘Isa and Muhammad – peace be upon them all.

learn.title: Ulul-‘azm – the determined messengers
learn.html: The most chosen of Allah’s messengers are Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, ‘Isa and Muhammad (peace be upon them).

learn.text: They lived from their own work

learn.html: Even though they were Allah’s messengers, they lived simply, from their own work: Muhammad (SAW) was a shepherd as a boy and later a trader; Dawud (AS) made armour; Sulayman (AS) was a builder; ‘Isa (AS) was a carpenter; Idris (AS) was a tailor.

items: Ibrahim (AS) was the father of Isma‘il (AS) and Ishaq (AS).
Ibrahim (AS) was the uncle of Lut (AS).
Ishaq (AS) was the father of Ya‘qub (AS), and Ya‘qub (AS) was the father of Yusuf (AS).
Zakariyya (AS) was the father of Yahya (AS).
Dawud (AS) was the father of Sulayman (AS).

learn.text: Muhammad (SAW) – the last and most chosen messenger (571–632)

learn.html: His father was Abdullah and his mother Aminah. His father died two months before he was born, and his mother when he was six. Then his grandfather Abdul-Muttalib looked after him, and after his grandfather his uncle Abu Talib. He stayed with his uncle until he was 25, when he married the respected widow Khadijah.

At 40 he became a messenger and Allah began to reveal the Qur’an to him. For three years he called people to Islam in secret, then openly. In the 13th year of the revelation he and the Muslims made the Hijrah – they moved from Makkah to Madinah. He passed away in 632, at the age of 63.

questions.q: What is the fourth pillar of Iman?
options: Wa rusulihi – belief in the messengers
Wa kutubihi – belief in the books
Wa malaa’ikatihi – belief in the angels
Wal-yawmil-aakhir – belief in the Last Day

questions.q: How many messengers are named in the Qur’an?

options: Adam, Idris, Hud, Salih and Lut
Dawud, Sulayman, Yunus, Yahya and Ilyas
Ishaq, Ya‘qub, Yusuf, Ayyub and Harun
